title: Expected encoding of an action
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $n,s$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ be a Boolean input of length $n$. Let $c$ be a configuration on input $x$, $t$ a codec row, $p$ a tuple of an input-head position and work-head positions, $q$ a case consisting of an optional state, an optional input symbol, and one optional symbol per work tape, and $a$ a Boolean assignment to the codec ports. Assume that the input head recorded in the row of $c$ is the input-head position in $p$, and that each work-tape head of $c$ is at the integer position represented by its corresponding position in $p$ (with offset $s$). For every codec bit $b$, the expected value of $b$ under the action determined by $q$, using the port values read from the row of $c$ and $t$ by the gate wiring, equals the observed value of $b$ in the configuration obtained by applying that action to $c$ after replacing its output by the encoding of its output summary.
